instruction: Configure the presentation so each slide automatically advances every 3 seconds during the slideshow.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1)

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting all slides to auto-advance after 3 seconds. The evaluator reads the PPTX file and checks if all 23 slides have automatic timing set to 3000ms (3 seconds). Custom getter extracts transition timing from slide XML, metric verifies all slides have the correct auto-advance setting.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator provides complete coverage - checks all 23 slides for auto-advance timing
Getter correctly extracts state by reading the advTm attribute from p:transition elements in slide XML, which is the correct location for LibreOffice Impress auto-advance settings
Metric uses appropriate comparison logic - exact equality check for timing values (auto_advance_ms == 3000)
Expected values are semantically correct: auto_advance_seconds=3 matches instruction requirement, num_slides=23 is correct for the presentation
Partial credit scoring is logical - calculates percentage of slides with correct timing
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) to ensure changes are persisted to disk
Robust error handling for edge cases: missing files, XML parsing errors, slides without auto-advance timing, empty results
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts PPTX → parses slide XML → reads advTm → returns timing data; metric compares timing for each slide → calculates score
